summary.en: HRPF requested repairs and maintenance for the Union Council building in Mianwal Ranjha to protect public property and support local services.

details.overview: HRPF raised concerns about the condition of the Union Council building in Mianwal Ranjha, District Mandi Bahauddin. In a letter dated 9 April 2026 to the Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department, the Foundation requested attention to maintenance, damaged furniture, closed washrooms and roof drainage, with the aim of protecting public property and supporting usable local-government services.
details.challenge: Deteriorating local-government premises required the attention of the department responsible for the facility.
details.approach: HRPF submitted a formal departmental complaint seeking attention to the building’s condition.
objectives: Seek attention to the condition of local-government premises.
activities: Submitted a representation to the Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department.
Requested building repairs, furniture replacement, functioning washrooms and roof drainage.
outcomes: A formal representation dated 9 April 2026 documents the concerns and requested remedial measures.
Completion of repairs or replacement work has not been confirmed.

milestones.title: Building-maintenance representation
milestones.description: HRPF requested departmental attention to the condition and upkeep of the Union Council building in Mianwal Ranjha.

images.caption: Request to the Local Government and Community Development Department concerning the Union Council building in Mianwal Ranjha.

summary.en: HRPF follows up police-related RTI requests and uses district crime records to support public-safety research and institutional accountability.

details.overview: HRPF uses lawful information requests and public-interest research to raise concerns about public safety and institutional accountability in Mandi Bahauddin. Its police-related RTI follow-up includes correspondence from December 2021 and proceedings before the Punjab Information Commission in March 2023. Separately, HRPF prepared an analysis of district crime records for January to August 2024 and shared concerns and recommendations with relevant officials and human-rights organisations.
details.challenge: Community concerns about crime and investigations required reliable information and an accountable institutional response.
details.approach: HRPF seeks public information through the Punjab Right to Information framework, follows up with the responsible public information officers and the Punjab Information Commission, and uses available records to prepare public-interest analysis and recommendations.
details.period: RTI follow-up in 2021–2023, crime analysis in 2024 and inquiry follow-up in 2025
details.targetCommunity: Communities seeking accountable policing and public safety
objectives: Use district records to inform public-safety advocacy.
activities: Submitted and followed up police-related requests for public information.
Pursued an RTI complaint before the Punjab Information Commission in March 2023.
Analysed district crime records covering January to August 2024.
Shared findings and recommendations with relevant officials and human-rights organisations.
Requested follow-up on a police inquiry report in February 2025.
outcomes: Police correspondence and Information Commission orders document the RTI follow-up process.
District crime analysis was prepared and communicated.
The available records do not confirm compliance with every information request or implementation of the recommended policing reforms.

milestones.title: Police response correspondence
milestones.description: The District Police Officer informed the Central Police Office that a reply had already been sent on 21 December. The enclosed reply is not included in the available material.

milestones.title: RTI complaint registered
milestones.description: The Punjab Information Commission registered the complaint and directed the police and traffic information officers to provide information or explain any lawful exemption.

milestones.title: Request forwarded for response
milestones.description: The Central Police Office forwarded the information request to the District Police Officer, Mandi Bahauddin.

milestones.title: Fresh notice issued
milestones.description: The Commission requested certified information within seven working days and scheduled further proceedings for 5 April 2023.

milestones.title: District crime analysis
milestones.description: HRPF prepared and shared analysis of district crime records covering January to August 2024.

milestones.title: Police inquiry follow-up requested
milestones.description: HRPF wrote to the Inspector General of Punjab Police asking for action on the inquiry report referred to in its representation. Subsequent action is not confirmed.

details.overview: HRPF raised concerns about road levels and waterlogging in Mianwal Ranjha. Its letter of 8 April 2026 to the Punjab Communication and Works Department reported that adjoining streets were lower than a recently constructed road and requested attention to water accumulation, roadside drainage and departmental responsibility. The Foundation also pursued the matter through the Provincial Ombudsman.
details.challenge: Waterlogging linked to road conditions created a public-service concern for local residents.
details.approach: HRPF submitted a departmental complaint and pursued the matter through the Provincial Ombudsman.
details.period: Representation dated 8 April 2026; subsequent complaint follow-up recorded in May 2026
details.targetCommunity: Residents affected by road drainage problems
objectives: Seek action on road drainage and waterlogging concerns.
activities: Submitted a road-level and drainage representation to the Communication and Works Department.
Requested cleaning, repair and restoration of roadside drainage.
outcomes: Repair completion and resolution of waterlogging are not confirmed.

milestones.title: Road-level and drainage representation
milestones.description: HRPF requested attention to road levels and drainage in Mianwal Ranjha.

images.alt: HRPF letter concerning road levels and drainage, 8 April 2026
images.caption: Request to the Communication and Works Department concerning street levels, water accumulation and drainage in Mianwal Ranjha.

details.overview: HRPF obtained district health data through a Right to Information request, analysed disease patterns in Sialkot and published recommendations for public-health action.
details.challenge: Public-service planning required a clearer picture of disease patterns and priorities for water, sanitation and healthcare.
details.approach: HRPF reviewed data supplied by the District Health Authority and prepared an analysis calling attention to public-health needs.
details.targetCommunity: Communities whose health needs inform public-service planning
objectives: Inform public-health planning through analysis of district records.
activities: Published recommendations for the responsible health authorities.
outcomes: A public-health analysis and recommendations were published.
The research does not establish that recommended services were subsequently delivered.

milestones.title: District Health Authority response
milestones.description: The District Health Authority, Sialkot, replied to HRPF’s information request and stated that district disease information was attached.

milestones.title: Public-health analysis shared
milestones.description: HRPF shared its health-status report covering January to April 2024.

images.alt: District Health Authority Sialkot RTI reply, 23 May 2024
images.caption: The District Health Authority replies to HRPF’s request for district disease information. The attached dataset is not part of this image.

details.overview: HRPF brought canal-pollution concerns before environmental authorities and the Provincial Ombudsman, seeking enforcement and departmental follow-up.
details.challenge: Reported sewage and poultry-waste discharge threatened the condition of fresh canal water and the surrounding environment.
details.approach: HRPF gathered information, approached the responsible departments and presented documentary evidence during Ombudsman proceedings.
details.targetCommunity: Communities relying on local canals and a healthy environment
objectives: Seek enforcement and departmental accountability for canal pollution.
activities: Reported pollution concerns to environmental and other relevant departments.
Presented supporting documents during Ombudsman proceedings.
Shared a public video appeal seeking environmental-authority attention to reported canal pollution and unsafe waste disposal.
outcomes: Show-cause notices and referrals for environmental proceedings were recorded.
Ombudsman directions called for departmental action and a follow-up report.
Long-term water-quality improvement is not measured in the available record.
